title: Kitty campaign: authoritative Work projection
description: First vertical slice: expose Builder truth through one Gateway-owned read-only Work projection. No second queue, store, scheduler, approval system, or execution state.

packets.title: Expose authoritative Gateway Work projection
packets.objective: Implement the first Kitty campaign vertical slice. Create gateway/work_projection.py as a pure dict-to-dict product-language mapper over gateway.builder_status.build_status_snapshot() output. Create gateway/routes/work.py with GET /work and register it in gateway/routes/register.py. The Work layer MUST NOT import sqlite3, gateway.builder_queue, gateway.builder_attempt, gateway.builder_initiative, or open Builder storage directly. It may only consume build_status_snapshot(). One Work item maps to one Builder initiative and carries source.kind=builder plus initiative identity. Product states must truthfully cover active (live run starting/running/cancel_requested), ready (eligible/queued), blocked, paused, failed, completed, and waiting. The current packet selection must prefer a live run, then initiative.next_packet, then a non-terminal packet, then the most recently updated packet. Expose blocker, next_action, current packet/run, validation/review/publication evidence from persisted snapshot facts only. Because no durable Gateway approval identity is bound to Builder initiatives yet, approval MUST be {state: unavailable, reason: ...binding...}; never reinterpret Builder awaiting_review as Jacob approval. A complete snapshot is source state available; partial integrity is degraded with an explicit reason. Include observed_at and valid_until with a 30-second freshness window. If build_status_snapshot() raises, GET /work MUST return HTTP 503 with a bounded concrete reason, never an empty-success list. Use TDD: write tests first, observe them fail for missing behavior, then implement minimally. Change nothing outside the allowed paths.
acceptance_criteria: GET /work returns schema-version-1 Work items derived only from build_status_snapshot() and the Work implementation contains no direct Builder DB/storage import.
Tests prove active, ready, blocked, paused, failed, completed, waiting, partial-integrity, unavailable-evidence, and approval-unavailable behavior.
A Builder snapshot exception produces HTTP 503 with the concrete bounded reason and never a successful empty Work payload.
Focused Work, Builder read-only, and architecture-fitness tests plus Ruff all exit 0.
